summary: Order API timestamps by parsing them, not by comparing bytes.
reason: The API renders the same field two ways, with a microsecond component and without it whenever that component is zero; a synced mirror held 235 of the first shape against 67 of the second. Compared as strings those invert, because '.' (0x2E) sorts below 'Z' (0x5A), so a whole-second value reads as later than a sub-second value in the same second. gate picked the wrong baseline eval run, resolveGateRevisionTag picked the wrong tagged revision, and changelog printed audit events from one action out of order. A shared apiTimeAfter helper now parses both sides; parseAPITime already existed and was already used correctly elsewhere in the same package.
validated_outcome: TestPickGateBaselineUsesRealTimeOrder selects the newer of two runs sharing a second; it fails against the byte comparison.
